concept_html:
Every analysis rests on assumptions: what a row means, how "don't know" is coded, which respondents are in scope, that weights sum to the sample size. Unwritten, they live in one analyst's head and break silently when the data changes.

Keep an assumptions log next to the analysis. One entry per assumption, with the same fields each time:

- id: A3
  statement: "score uses 1 to 10; 98 = refused, 99 = don't know"
  evidence: "Questionnaire v4, Q12; profile of waves 1 to 11 shows only 1-10, 98, 99"
  handling: "98 and 99 become missing before any statistic"
  check: "score in 1..10 or missing, after recoding"
  owner: "analysis team"
  last_verified: 2026-09-01

Then make the assumption executable. The handling becomes code, and the check becomes a QA result (lesson B5-L3) that runs on every delivery.

MISSING_CODES: dict[str, list[int]] = {"score": [98, 99]}   # from config, per A3


def recode_missing(df: pd.DataFrame, codes: dict[str, list[int]]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return df.assign(**{col: df[col].mask(df[col].isin(vals)) for col, vals in codes.items()})

Recode per column. df.replace(99, np.nan) on the whole frame also blanks a real age of 99. Series.mask(cond) sets values to missing where the condition holds and leaves the rest.

Three kinds of assumption to write down every time:

  • Structure. Grain, keys, which columns are required.
  • Coding. Missing codes, scales, units, category lists.
  • Scope. Who is included: age limits, completes only, which markets and waves.

When a check fails, the log tells you which belief was wrong and who to ask. When a client asks "why is this respondent excluded?", the answer has an ID.

lines: import pandas as pd
def recode_missing(df: pd.DataFrame, codes: dict[str, list[int]]) -> pd.DataFrame:
"""Set listed codes to missing, per column (assumption A3). Other columns untouched."""
return df.assign(**{col: df[col].mask(df[col].isin(vals)) for col, vals in codes.items()})
def score_in_range(df: pd.DataFrame, low: int, high: int) -> bool:
"""Check for A3: every non-missing score lies in [low, high]."""
s = df["score"].dropna()
return bool(s.between(low, high).all())

import pandas as pd


def recode_missing(df: pd.DataFrame, codes: dict[str, list[int]]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Set listed codes to missing, per column.

    Args:
        df: Input frame.
        codes: Column name to the values that mean missing in that column.

    Returns:
        A new frame. Unlisted columns are unchanged.
    """
    return df.assign(**{col: df[col].mask(df[col].isin(vals)) for col, vals in codes.items()})

title: Write assumptions down, then turn them into checks
why_html:
An analyst knew that 99 meant "don't know" on the satisfaction scale and removed those rows by hand in a notebook. The analyst left. The next wave went through the scripted pipeline, which did not know. The regional mean rose from 7.1 to 11.4. It was published, because 11.4 looked like a large improvement rather than an impossible value on a 1 to 10 scale.

A logged assumption with an executable check would have failed the run on the first 99.
